summary: Iter79 retest of iter78 P0/P1 blockers + new WhatsApp dedup feature. ALL 36 backend tests PASS (35 from requested suites + 1 supplemental copie 3 regression). P0 cross-tenant leak on /admin/appointments is FIXED (tenant A no longer sees LEAK-TEST for SAWALI SMART SYSTEMS-Client, tenant B no longer sees LEAK-TEST for ISISPHARMA, super-admin sees both). Same pattern verified on /admin/interventions and /admin/documents. P1 recipe duplication suffix incrementation FIXED (re.escape applied) — three successive POST /production/recipes/{rid}/duplicate correctly return (copie), (copie 2), (copie 3). NEW WhatsApp inbound dedup: same wa_message_id posted twice persists ONLY 1 row, different ids from same phone persist 2 rows, sparse index wa_message_id_sparse present on db.whatsapp_messages. Regression suites test_iter43_fix24az_f_production.py (8) + test_iter43_fix24az_k_vidal_webhook.py (6) still green.
critical_code_review_comments: Both P0/P1 fixes match the exact recommendations from iter78 RCA (server.py admin_* endpoints now go through _is_super_admin/_resolve_visible_client_ids scoping ; routes/production.py uses re.escape() on the candidate before the regex uniqueness pre-check). No further code changes required.
The new WhatsApp dedup uses a sparse unique-lookup approach (index wa_message_id_sparse) which is correct — avoids penalizing legacy rows without wa_message_id.

Suggestion for a future iteration: consider adding a static-analysis grep guard in CI to flag any new admin_* endpoint that does db.<coll>.find({}) without a scope helper — the leak pattern is easy to reintroduce.
seed_data_creation: None persistent — all test copies of recipes and TEST_ intrants deleted in teardown ; WhatsApp fixture rows deleted after each test.

rca of the issue: Both iter78 blockers now RESOLVED and validated. P0 fix : admin_appointments (server.py:7768-7781), admin_interventions (7822-7830), admin_documents (7920-7942) all now branch on _is_super_admin() and, for non-super-admins, filter by _resolve_visible_client_ids() — matching the pattern used in /me/notes/*.
